For the original equiconvex lens, the focal length $f$ is given by $\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{2}{R}\right)$.

When cut perpendicular to the principal axis, the resulting plano-convex lens has a focal length $f_l$ given by $\dfrac{1}{f_l} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R}\right)$. Thus, $f_l = 2f$.

When the plane surface is silvered, the system behaves as an equivalent mirror. Light passes through the lens, reflects from the mirror, and passes through the lens again. The equivalent power is $P_{eq} = 2P_l + P_m$.

The power of the lens is $P_l = \dfrac{1}{f_l} = \dfrac{1}{2f}$ and the power of the plane mirror is $P_m = 0$ (since its radius of curvature is $\infty$).

Therefore, $P_{eq} = 2\left(\dfrac{1}{2f}\right) + 0 = \dfrac{1}{f}$.

The magnitude of the equivalent focal length is $F = \dfrac{1}{P_{eq}} = f$. The system behaves as a concave mirror of focal length $f$.

Answer: $f$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two thin lenses are placed in contact such that the equivalent focal length of the combination is $+50\text{ cm}$. If one of the lenses is a convex lens of focal length $20\text{ cm}$, what is the focal length and nature of the second lens?
options: Concave lens of focal length $\dfrac{100}{3}\text{ cm}$
Convex lens of focal length $\dfrac{100}{3}\text{ cm}$
Convex lens of focal length $30\text{ cm}$
Convex lens of focal length $\dfrac{100}{7}\text{ cm}$
questions.solution:
Let the equivalent focal length of the combination be $F_{eq}$ and the focal lengths of the individual lenses be $f_1$ and $f_2$.

Given:
$F_{eq} = +50\text{ cm}$
$f_1 = +20\text{ cm}$ (since it is a convex lens)

The formula for the equivalent focal length of thin lenses in contact is:
$\dfrac{1}{F_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{f_1} + \dfrac{1}{f_2}$

Substituting the given values:
$\dfrac{1}{50} = \dfrac{1}{20} + \dfrac{1}{f_2}$

$\dfrac{1}{f_2} = \dfrac{1}{50} - \dfrac{1}{20}$

$\dfrac{1}{f_2} = \dfrac{2 - 5}{100} = -\dfrac{3}{100}\text{ cm}^{-1}$

$f_2 = -\dfrac{100}{3}\text{ cm}$

The negative sign indicates that the second lens is a concave lens. Therefore, it is a concave lens of focal length $\dfrac{100}{3}\text{ cm}$.

Answer: Concave lens of focal length $\dfrac{100}{3}\text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A point object is placed at a distance of $15\text{ cm}$ from a convex lens of unknown focal length. A concave mirror of focal length $10\text{ cm}$ is placed $30\text{ cm}$ behind the lens, coaxial with it. It is observed that the light rays retrace their path after reflection from the mirror, such that the final image coincides with the object. The focal length of the convex lens is:
questions.solution:
For the light rays to retrace their path after reflection from the concave mirror, they must strike the mirror normally. This implies that the rays must appear to come from the center of curvature of the concave mirror.

The radius of curvature of the concave mirror is $R = 2f_m = 2 \times 10\text{ cm} = 20\text{ cm}$.

Thus, the convex lens must form the first image of the object at the center of curvature of the mirror, which is $20\text{ cm}$ in front of the mirror.

Given the distance between the lens and the mirror is $30\text{ cm}$, the image distance from the lens is:
$v = 30\text{ cm} - 20\text{ cm} = +10\text{ cm}$

For the convex lens, the object distance is $u = -15\text{ cm}$.

Using the lens formula:
$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u}$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{-15} = \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{15}$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{3 + 2}{30} = \dfrac{5}{30} = \dfrac{1}{6}$

$f = +6\text{ cm}$

Answer: $6\text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A right-angled thin prism of angle $6^{\circ}$ and refractive index $1.5$ is completely immersed in a transparent liquid of refractive index $1.2$. A light ray is incident normally on the vertical face of the prism. The angle of emergence of the ray into the liquid from the inclined face is
questions.solution:
Since the light ray is incident normally on the vertical face, the angle of incidence $i_{1} = 0^{\circ}$, which means the angle of refraction $r_{1} = 0^{\circ}$.

The angle of the prism is $A = r_{1} + r_{2}$, so the angle of incidence at the second (inclined) face is $r_{2} = A = 6^{\circ}$.

Applying Snell's law at the second interface (from prism to liquid) and using the small angle approximation:
$\mu_{P} \times r_{2} = \mu_{L} \times e$
$\mu_{P} \times A = \mu_{L} \times e$

Substituting the given values ($\mu_{P} = 1.5$, $\mu_{L} = 1.2$, $A = 6^{\circ}$):
$1.5 \times 6^{\circ} = 1.2 \times e$
$e = \dfrac{1.5}{1.2} \times 6^{\circ} = 1.25 \times 6^{\circ} = 7.5^{\circ}$

Answer: $7.5^{\circ}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two thin lenses, one convex of focal length magnitude $f_1$ and one concave of focal length magnitude $f_2$, are placed in contact. What is the necessary condition for this combination to behave as a converging lens?
questions.solution:
The equivalent power of two thin lenses in contact is the algebraic sum of their individual powers: $P_{eq} = P_1 + P_2$.

The power of a lens is the reciprocal of its focal length. For a convex lens, power is positive ($P_1 = \dfrac{1}{f_1}$), and for a concave lens, power is negative ($P_2 = -\dfrac{1}{f_2}$).

Thus, the equivalent power of the combination is $P_{eq} = \dfrac{1}{f_1} - \dfrac{1}{f_2}$.

For the combination to behave as a converging lens, its equivalent power must be positive ($P_{eq} \gt 0$).

$\dfrac{1}{f_1} - \dfrac{1}{f_2} \gt 0 \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{f_1} \gt \dfrac{1}{f_2}$

Since $f_1$ and $f_2$ are positive magnitudes, taking the reciprocal reverses the inequality, which simplifies to $f_1 \lt f_2$.

Answer: $f_1 \lt f_2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An equiconcave lens made of glass with a refractive index of $1.5$ has a power of $-5\text{ D}$. The magnitude of the radius of curvature of each of its surfaces is:
questions.solution:
The power of a lens is related to its focal length by $P = \dfrac{1}{f}$, where $f$ is in meters.

Using the Lens Maker's formula:

$P = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$

For an equiconcave lens, by sign convention, the first surface is concave ($R_1 = -R$) and the second surface is convex towards the incident light from inside the lens ($R_2 = +R$).

Substituting the values into the formula:

$-5 = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{-R} - \dfrac{1}{R}\right)$

$-5 = 0.5 \times \left(\dfrac{-2}{R}\right)$

$-5 = \dfrac{-1}{R}$

$R = \dfrac{1}{5}\text{ m}$

Converting to centimeters:

$R = 0.2\text{ m} = 20\text{ cm}$

The magnitude of the radius of curvature is $20\text{ cm}$.

Answer: $20\text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An equiconvex lens of power $P$ is cut into two identical halves by a plane perpendicular to its principal axis. The power of one of the resulting halves will be
questions.solution:
For an equiconvex lens, the power is given by Lens Maker's formula as $P = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \left(-\dfrac{1}{R}\right)\right) = \dfrac{2(\mu - 1)}{R}$.

When the lens is cut by a plane perpendicular to the principal axis, each half becomes a plano-convex lens. The radii of curvature for one of these halves are $R$ and $\infty$.

The power of this new plano-convex lens is $P' = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right) = \dfrac{\mu - 1}{R}$.

Comparing the two expressions, we get $P' = \dfrac{P}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{P}{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In an astronomical telescope, the length of the telescope tube is maximum when the final image is formed at the least distance of distinct vision.
Reason (R): For the final image to form at the least distance of distinct vision, the intermediate image formed by the objective must lie between the eyepiece and its principal focus.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
The length of an astronomical telescope tube is given by $L = f_o + u_e$, where $u_e$ is the distance of the intermediate image from the eyepiece.

In normal adjustment (final image at infinity), the intermediate image is formed at the principal focus of the eyepiece, so $u_e = f_e$.

When the final image is formed at the least distance of distinct vision ($D$), the eyepiece acts as a simple magnifier forming a virtual, erect (with respect to the intermediate image) and magnified image. For a convex lens to form a virtual image, the object must lie between the optical centre and the principal focus. Thus, $u_e \lt f_e$. This makes Reason (R) true.

Since $u_e$ is smaller than $f_e$ in this adjustment, the tube length $L = f_o + u_e$ is minimum at the near point adjustment, whereas it is maximum in normal adjustment. Therefore, Assertion (A) is false.

Answer: (A) is false but (R) is true.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A point object is placed at a distance of $30\text{ cm}$ from a convex lens of focal length $20\text{ cm}$. A convex mirror of radius of curvature $40\text{ cm}$ is placed coaxially at a distance of $40\text{ cm}$ behind the lens. The position of the final image formed after reflection from the mirror and subsequent refraction through the lens is:
options: $20\text{ cm}$ from the lens on the side of the object
$60\text{ cm}$ from the lens on the side opposite to the object
$60\text{ cm}$ from the lens on the side of the object
questions.solution:
For the first refraction through the convex lens:
$u_1 = -30\text{ cm}$, $f_L = +20\text{ cm}$

Using the lens formula:
$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{f_L}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{-30} = \dfrac{1}{20} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_1} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{60}$

$v_1 = +60\text{ cm}$

The first image is formed $60\text{ cm}$ behind the lens. Since the convex mirror is placed $40\text{ cm}$ behind the lens, this image acts as a virtual object for the mirror, located $20\text{ cm}$ behind it.

For the reflection from the convex mirror:
$u_M = +20\text{ cm}$ (virtual object)
The focal length of the convex mirror is $f_M = \dfrac{R}{2} = \dfrac{+40\text{ cm}}{2} = +20\text{ cm}$.

Using the mirror formula:
$\dfrac{1}{v_M} + \dfrac{1}{u_M} = \dfrac{1}{f_M}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_M} + \dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{1}{20} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_M} = 0$

$v_M = \infty$

The rays reflected by the convex mirror become parallel to the principal axis.

For the second refraction through the convex lens:
The parallel rays ($u_2 = -\infty$) fall on the lens and will converge at its principal focus.

$v_2 = f_L = 20\text{ cm}$

Since the light is now traveling in the reverse direction (from the mirror to the lens), the final image is formed $20\text{ cm}$ from the lens on the side of the original object.

Answer: $20\text{ cm}$ from the lens on the side of the object

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ray of light is incident at an angle of $45^{\circ}$ on one face of a prism of refracting angle $30^{\circ}$. The opposite face of the prism is silvered. If the ray retraces its path after reflection from the silvered face, the refractive index of the material of the prism is
questions.solution:
For the ray to retrace its path, it must strike the silvered face normally. Thus, the angle of incidence at the second face is $r_2 = 0^{\circ}$.

For a prism, the refracting angle $A = r_1 + r_2$.
Given $A = 30^{\circ}$, we have $30^{\circ} = r_1 + 0^{\circ} \Rightarrow r_1 = 30^{\circ}$.

Applying Snell's law at the first face:
$\mu_1 \sin i = \mu_2 \sin r_1$
$1 \times \sin 45^{\circ} = \mu \times \sin 30^{\circ}$
$\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \mu \times \dfrac{1}{2}$
$\mu = \sqrt{2}$

Answer: $\sqrt{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the ratio of apparent depth (or height) to real depth (or height) for different combinations of observer and object media. Assume near normal viewing. The refractive indices are: Air ($n=1$), Water ($n=4/3$), and Glass ($n=3/2$).

List-IList-II
A. Observer in Air, Object in Water1. $4/3$
B. Observer in Water, Object in Air2. $3/4$
C. Observer in Glass, Object in Water3. $8/9$
D. Observer in Water, Object in Glass4. $9/8$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The ratio of apparent depth (or height) to real depth (or height) is given by the formula:

$\dfrac{h_{\text{app}}}{h_{\text{real}}} = \dfrac{n_{\text{observer}}}{n_{\text{object}}}$

For A: Observer in Air ($n=1$), Object in Water ($n=4/3$).
Ratio = $\dfrac{1}{4/3} = \dfrac{3}{4}$. So, A matches with 2.

For B: Observer in Water ($n=4/3$), Object in Air ($n=1$).
Ratio = $\dfrac{4/3}{1} = \dfrac{4}{3}$. So, B matches with 1.

For C: Observer in Glass ($n=3/2$), Object in Water ($n=4/3$).
Ratio = $\dfrac{3/2}{4/3} = \dfrac{9}{8}$. So, C matches with 4.

For D: Observer in Water ($n=4/3$), Object in Glass ($n=3/2$).
Ratio = $\dfrac{4/3}{3/2} = \dfrac{8}{9}$. So, D matches with 3.

The correct matching is A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3.

Answer: A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II for the equivalent focal length of two thin lenses placed in contact. The focal lengths of the lenses are given in terms of a positive magnitude $f$.

List-I (Lens combination)List-II (Equivalent focal length)
A. Convex $f$ and Convex $f$I. $f$
B. Convex $f$ and Concave $f$II. $-f$
C. Convex $f$ and Concave $f/2$III. Infinite
D. Convex $f/2$ and Concave $f$IV. $f/2$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
For two thin lenses in contact, the equivalent focal length $F$ is given by $\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{f_1} + \dfrac{1}{f_2}$.

By sign convention, the focal length of a convex lens is positive, and that of a concave lens is negative.

A. Convex $f$ and Convex $f$: $\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{2}{f} \Rightarrow F = \dfrac{f}{2}$ (Matches IV)

B. Convex $f$ and Concave $f$: $\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{f} = 0 \Rightarrow F = \infty$ (Matches III)

C. Convex $f$ and Concave $f/2$: $\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{2}{f} = -\dfrac{1}{f} \Rightarrow F = -f$ (Matches II)

D. Convex $f/2$ and Concave $f$: $\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{2}{f} - \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{f} \Rightarrow F = f$ (Matches I)

Therefore, the correct matching is A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I.

Answer: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ray of light is incident at a grazing angle (angle of incidence $90^\circ$) on one face of a glass prism. The refracting angle of the prism is $75^\circ$ and the refractive index of the glass is $\sqrt{2}$. What is the angle of emergence of the ray from the second face of the prism?
questions.solution:
At the first face, applying Snell's law for grazing incidence ($i = 90^\circ$):
$1 \times \sin(90^\circ) = \mu \sin(r_1)$
$1 = \sqrt{2} \sin(r_1) \Rightarrow \sin(r_1) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \Rightarrow r_1 = 45^\circ$

Using the prism relation for the refracting angle, $r_1 + r_2 = A$:
$45^\circ + r_2 = 75^\circ \Rightarrow r_2 = 30^\circ$

At the second face, applying Snell's law to find the angle of emergence $e$:
$\mu \sin(r_2) = 1 \times \sin(e)$
$\sqrt{2} \sin(30^\circ) = \sin(e)$
$\sqrt{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \sin(e) \Rightarrow \sin(e) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Therefore, the angle of emergence is $e = 45^\circ$.

Answer: $45^\circ$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two thin lenses of powers $+12 \text{ D}$ and $-2 \text{ D}$ are placed in contact coaxially. An object is placed at a distance of $15 \text{ cm}$ from this combination. The linear magnification produced by the combination is
questions.solution:
Effective power of the combination, $P_{\text{net}} = P_1 + P_2$

$P_{\text{net}} = +12 \text{ D} + (-2 \text{ D}) = +10 \text{ D}$

Effective focal length, $f_{\text{net}} = \dfrac{100}{P_{\text{net}}} \text{ cm} = \dfrac{100}{10} \text{ cm} = +10 \text{ cm}$

Given object distance, $u = -15 \text{ cm}$ (using sign convention)

Using the formula for linear magnification in terms of focal length and object distance:

$m = \dfrac{f_{\text{net}}}{f_{\text{net}} + u}$

$m = \dfrac{10}{10 + (-15)} = \dfrac{10}{-5} = -2$

Thus, the linear magnification produced is $-2$.

Answer: $-2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An equiconvex lens made of glass (refractive index $1.5$) has a power of $+5 \text{ D}$ in air. If this lens is completely immersed in water (refractive index $\dfrac{4}{3}$), what will be its new focal length?
questions.solution:
The focal length of the lens in air is given by:
$f_a = \dfrac{100}{P_a} = \dfrac{100}{5} = 20 \text{ cm}$

Using the Lens Maker's formula in air:
$\dfrac{1}{f_a} = (\mu_g - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$
For an equiconvex lens, $R_1 = R$ and $R_2 = -R$.
$\dfrac{1}{20} = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{2}{R}\right) \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{20} = 0.5 \times \dfrac{2}{R} \Rightarrow R = 20 \text{ cm}$

When the lens is immersed in water, the relative refractive index of glass with respect to water is $\mu_{gw} = \dfrac{\mu_g}{\mu_w}$.
The new focal length $f_w$ is:
$\dfrac{1}{f_w} = \left(\dfrac{\mu_g}{\mu_w} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{2}{R}\right)$
$\dfrac{1}{f_w} = \left(\dfrac{1.5}{4/3} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{2}{20}\right) = \left(\dfrac{9}{8} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{10}\right)$
$\dfrac{1}{f_w} = \left(\dfrac{1}{8}\right) \times \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{1}{80}$

$f_w = +80 \text{ cm}$

Answer: $+80 \text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two lenses, A and B, are made of the same transparent material. Lens A is an equiconvex lens, while lens B is a plano-convex lens. If the curved surfaces of both lenses have the same radius of curvature, what is the ratio of the power of lens A to the power of lens B?
questions.solution:
Let the radius of curvature of the curved surfaces be $R$ and the refractive index of the material be $\mu$.

For the equiconvex lens A, the radii of curvature are $R_{1} = R$ and $R_{2} = -R$.
The power of lens A is:
$P_{A} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{-R}\right) = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{2}{R}\right)$

For the plano-convex lens B, the radii of curvature are $R_{1} = R$ and $R_{2} = \infty$.
The power of lens B is:
$P_{B} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right) = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R}\right)$

The ratio of their powers is:
$\dfrac{P_{A}}{P_{B}} = \dfrac{2(\mu - 1)/R}{(\mu - 1)/R} = \dfrac{2}{1}$

Thus, the ratio is $2:1$.

Answer: $2:1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A concave mirror of focal length $10\text{ cm}$ and a plane mirror are placed facing each other, separated by a distance of $20\text{ cm}$ along their common principal axis. A small linear object is placed exactly midway between them, perpendicular to the axis. Consider the image formation process where light from the object first reflects from the plane mirror and then from the concave mirror. Read the following statements:
(A) The image formed by the plane mirror acts as a virtual object for the concave mirror.
(B) The first image is formed $30\text{ cm}$ away from the pole of the concave mirror.
(C) The final image is formed $15\text{ cm}$ from the concave mirror.
(D) The final image is real and inverted with respect to the original object.

How many of the given statements are correct?
questions.solution:
The object is at $10\text{ cm}$ from the plane mirror. The plane mirror forms a virtual image $I_1$ at $10\text{ cm}$ behind it.

Statement (A) is incorrect: The rays from $I_1$ diverge towards the concave mirror. Therefore, $I_1$ acts as a real object for the concave mirror, not a virtual object.

Statement (B) is correct: The distance of $I_1$ from the concave mirror is the separation between the mirrors plus the distance of $I_1$ behind the plane mirror $= 20\text{ cm} + 10\text{ cm} = 30\text{ cm}$.

Statement (C) is correct: For the concave mirror, $u = -30\text{ cm}$ and $f = -10\text{ cm}$.
Using the mirror formula: $\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v} = -\dfrac{1}{10} - \left(-\dfrac{1}{30}\right) = -\dfrac{2}{30} \Rightarrow v = -15\text{ cm}$.
The final image is formed $15\text{ cm}$ in front of the concave mirror.

Statement (D) is correct: The magnification of the concave mirror is $m_2 = -\dfrac{v}{u} = -\dfrac{-15}{-30} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$. The plane mirror has $m_1 = +1$. Total magnification $m = m_1 \times m_2 = -\dfrac{1}{2}$. Since $m$ is negative and $v$ is negative, the final image is real and inverted.

Thus, exactly 3 statements are correct.

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An equilateral prism made of a material of refractive index $2$ is completely immersed in a transparent liquid of refractive index $\sqrt{2}$. A ray of monochromatic light is incident on one face of the prism such that the refracted ray inside the prism travels parallel to its base. What is the angle of incidence of the ray at the prism face?
questions.solution:
For an equilateral prism, the angle of the prism is $A = 60^\circ$.

When the refracted ray inside the prism is parallel to its base, the prism is in the position of minimum deviation.

In this position, the angle of refraction at the first face is $r = \dfrac{A}{2} = \dfrac{60^\circ}{2} = 30^\circ$.

Applying Snell's law at the first refracting surface, we use the relative refractive index of the prism with respect to the surrounding liquid:

$\mu_{\text{liquid}} \sin i = \mu_{\text{prism}} \sin r$

Substituting the given values ($\mu_{\text{liquid}} = \sqrt{2}$, $\mu_{\text{prism}} = 2$):

$\sqrt{2} \sin i = 2 \sin 30^\circ$

$\sqrt{2} \sin i = 2 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 1$

$\sin i = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Therefore, the angle of incidence is $i = 45^\circ$.

Answer: $45^\circ$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A light ray is incident normally on one of the mutually perpendicular faces of a right-angled thin prism. The refractive index of the material of the prism is $1.6$. If the ray emerges from the inclined face at an angle of $8^{\circ}$ with respect to the normal of that face, the angle of the prism is
questions.solution:
For normal incidence on the first face, the angle of incidence $i_{1} = 0^{\circ}$, which implies the angle of refraction $r_{1} = 0^{\circ}$.

For a prism, the angle of the prism $A = r_{1} + r_{2}$. Therefore, the angle of incidence at the second face is $r_{2} = A$.

Applying Snell's law at the second face (from prism to air) and using the small angle approximation for a thin prism:
$\mu \times r_{2} = 1 \times e$
$\mu \times A = e$

Substituting the given values ($\mu = 1.6$ and $e = 8^{\circ}$):
$1.6 \times A = 8^{\circ}$
$A = \dfrac{8^{\circ}}{1.6} = 5^{\circ}$

Answer: $5^{\circ}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A transparent solid slab of refractive index $1.5$ rests on a pool of transparent liquid of refractive index $2.0$. A small air bubble is trapped inside the solid slab. When viewed normally from the air above the slab, the apparent depth of the bubble is $4\text{ cm}$. When viewed normally from the liquid below the slab, the apparent depth of the bubble is $6\text{ cm}$. The actual total thickness of the solid slab is:
questions.solution:
Let the actual distance of the bubble from the top surface of the slab be $x_1$ and from the bottom surface be $x_2$.

The formula for apparent depth is given by:
$h_{\text{app}} = h_{\text{actual}} \times \dfrac{n_{\text{observer}}}{n_{\text{object}}}$

When viewed from the top (observer in air, $n_{\text{air}} = 1$):
$4 = x_1 \times \dfrac{1}{1.5}$
$x_1 = 4 \times 1.5 = 6\text{ cm}$

When viewed from the bottom (observer in liquid, $n_{\text{liquid}} = 2.0$):
$6 = x_2 \times \dfrac{2.0}{1.5}$
$x_2 = 6 \times \dfrac{1.5}{2.0} = 4.5\text{ cm}$

The total actual thickness of the solid slab is the sum of these two distances:
$\text{Thickness} = x_1 + x_2 = 6 + 4.5 = 10.5\text{ cm}$

Answer: $10.5\text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An equiconvex lens of refractive index $1.5$ has a radius of curvature of $30\text{ cm}$ for both of its surfaces. If one of the curved surfaces is silvered, what is the effective focal length of this arrangement?
questions.solution:
The silvered lens acts as an equivalent mirror. Light passes through the lens, reflects off the silvered back surface, and passes through the lens again.
The equivalent power is given by $P_{eq} = 2P_l + P_m$.

First, calculate the focal length of the unsilvered lens ($f_l$):
$\dfrac{1}{f_l} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right) = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{30} - \dfrac{1}{-30}\right) = 0.5 \times \dfrac{2}{30} = \dfrac{1}{30}\text{ cm}^{-1}$
The power of the lens is $P_l = \dfrac{1}{f_l} = \dfrac{1}{30}\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

The silvered back surface acts as a concave mirror to the light inside the lens. Its radius of curvature is $R = -30\text{ cm}$.
The focal length of this mirror is $f_m = \dfrac{R}{2} = -15\text{ cm}$.
The power of the mirror is $P_m = -\dfrac{1}{f_m} = -\dfrac{1}{-15} = \dfrac{1}{15}\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

Now, find the equivalent power:
$P_{eq} = 2\left(\dfrac{1}{30}\right) + \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{1}{15} + \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{2}{15}\text{ cm}^{-1}$

The effective focal length of the system is:
$F = -\dfrac{1}{P_{eq}} = -\dfrac{15}{2} = -7.5\text{ cm}$

Answer: $-7.5\text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object is placed at a distance of $40\text{ cm}$ from a combination of two thin lenses in contact. The combination forms a real and inverted image of the same size as the object. If the power of one of the lenses is $+10\text{ D}$, what is the power of the second lens?
questions.solution:
For a real and inverted image of the same size as the object, the linear magnification $m = -1$.

Using the magnification formula $m = \dfrac{v}{u}$:
$-1 = \dfrac{v}{-40\text{ cm}} \implies v = +40\text{ cm}$.

Applying the lens formula for the combination:
$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u}$
$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{40} - \dfrac{1}{-40} = \dfrac{2}{40} = \dfrac{1}{20}\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

The effective focal length of the combination is $F = +20\text{ cm} = +0.2\text{ m}$.

The effective power of the combination is:
$P_{\text{net}} = \dfrac{1}{F (\text{in m})} = \dfrac{1}{0.2} = +5\text{ D}$.

The effective power is the sum of the individual powers:
$P_{\text{net}} = P_1 + P_2$
$+5\text{ D} = +10\text{ D} + P_2$
$P_2 = -5\text{ D}$.

Answer: $-5\text{ D}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II for an equiconvex lens of power $P$.

List-I (Modification)List-II (Resulting Power)
(A) Cut into two equal halves along the principal axis (power of one part)(I) $\dfrac{P}{2}$
(B) Cut into two equal halves perpendicular to the principal axis (power of one part)(II) $0$
(C) Immersed in a liquid having the same refractive index as the lens material(III) $P$
(D) Two identical lenses placed in contact coaxially(IV) $2P$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) When cut along the principal axis, the radii of curvature remain unchanged. Hence, the focal length and power remain the same ($P$).

(B) When cut perpendicular to the principal axis, the lens becomes plano-convex. One radius of curvature becomes infinity, doubling the focal length and halving the power ($\dfrac{P}{2}$).

(C) When immersed in a liquid of the same refractive index, the relative refractive index becomes 1. The lens acts as a plane glass plate with infinite focal length and zero power ($0$).

(D) When two identical lenses are placed in contact, their equivalent power is the algebraic sum of their individual powers ($P + P = 2P$).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A convex lens of focal length $20\text{ cm}$ and a concave lens of focal length $10\text{ cm}$ are placed in contact. An object is placed $40\text{ cm}$ in front of this lens combination. At what distance from the combination will the image be formed?
options: $40\text{ cm}$ on the same side as the object
$\dfrac{40}{3}\text{ cm}$ on the same side as the object
$\dfrac{40}{3}\text{ cm}$ on the opposite side of the object
$8\text{ cm}$ on the opposite side of the object
questions.solution:
First, find the equivalent focal length ($F_{eq}$) of the lens combination.
For the convex lens, $f_1 = +20\text{ cm}$.
For the concave lens, $f_2 = -10\text{ cm}$.

$\dfrac{1}{F_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{f_1} + \dfrac{1}{f_2}$
$\dfrac{1}{F_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{1 - 2}{20} = -\dfrac{1}{20}\text{ cm}^{-1}$
So, $F_{eq} = -20\text{ cm}$ (the combination acts as a concave lens).

Next, apply the thin lens formula to find the image position ($v$).
Object distance, $u = -40\text{ cm}$.

$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{F_{eq}}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{-40} = \dfrac{1}{-20}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{40} = -\dfrac{1}{20}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = -\dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{40} = \dfrac{-2 - 1}{40} = -\dfrac{3}{40}\text{ cm}^{-1}$

$v = -\dfrac{40}{3}\text{ cm}$

The negative sign indicates that the image is formed on the same side as the object, at a distance of $\dfrac{40}{3}\text{ cm}$ from the lens combination.

Answer: $\dfrac{40}{3}\text{ cm}$ on the same side as the object

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A ray of light is incident normally on one face of an equilateral glass prism. Consider the following statements regarding the path of the ray:

I. The angle of incidence at the second face is $60^{\circ}$.
II. For the ray to emerge from the second face, the refractive index of the prism must be less than or equal to $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$.
III. If the refractive index of the prism is $1.5$, the ray undergoes total internal reflection at the second face.
IV. If the refractive index of the prism is $\sqrt{2}$, the ray emerges grazing the second face.

Choose the correct combination of valid statements:
questions.solution:
Since the ray is incident normally on the first face, $i_1 = 0^{\circ}$, which means the angle of refraction at the first face $r_1 = 0^{\circ}$.

For a prism, $r_1 + r_2 = A$. For an equilateral prism, $A = 60^{\circ}$. Thus, the angle of incidence at the second face $r_2 = 60^{\circ} - 0^{\circ} = 60^{\circ}$. (Statement I is correct)

For the ray to emerge, $r_2 \le C$, where $C$ is the critical angle.
$\sin(60^{\circ}) \le \sin C = \dfrac{1}{\mu}$
$\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \le \dfrac{1}{\mu} \Rightarrow \mu \le \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 1.15$. (Statement II is correct)

If $\mu = 1.5$, it is greater than $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$. Hence, the angle of incidence ($60^{\circ}$) is greater than the critical angle, and the ray undergoes total internal reflection. (Statement III is correct)

If $\mu = \sqrt{2} \approx 1.414$, it is also greater than $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$, so the ray will undergo total internal reflection. It will not emerge grazing the second face (which only happens if $\mu = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$). (Statement IV is incorrect)

Answer: I, II and III only

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A plano-convex lens of refractive index $1.5$ has a radius of curvature of $20\text{ cm}$ for its curved surface. If its plane surface is silvered, what will be the effective focal length of the resulting system?
questions.solution:
The silvered lens acts as an equivalent mirror.

The power of the equivalent mirror is given by:
$P_{eq} = 2P_{l} + P_{m}$

The focal length of the plano-convex lens $f_{l}$ is:
$\dfrac{1}{f_{l}} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right)$
$\dfrac{1}{f_{l}} = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{20} - 0\right) = \dfrac{0.5}{20} = \dfrac{1}{40}\text{ cm}^{-1}$

The power of the lens is $P_{l} = \dfrac{1}{f_{l}} = \dfrac{1}{40}\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

Since the plane surface is silvered, it acts as a plane mirror with an infinite radius of curvature. Its focal length $f_{m} = \infty$, so its power $P_{m} = 0$.

The equivalent power of the system is:
$P_{eq} = 2\left(\dfrac{1}{40}\right) + 0 = \dfrac{1}{20}\text{ cm}^{-1}$

The effective focal length $F$ of the system is:
$F = -\dfrac{1}{P_{eq}} = -20\text{ cm}$

Answer: $-20\text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An amateur astronomer designs an astronomical telescope in normal adjustment. The total tube length of the telescope is $105 \mathrm{~cm}$ and its magnifying power has a magnitude of $20$. What are the optical powers of the objective and the eyepiece lenses respectively?
questions.solution:
For an astronomical telescope in normal adjustment, the magnitude of magnifying power is given by:
$|m| = \dfrac{f_o}{f_e} = 20 \Rightarrow f_o = 20 f_e$

The tube length is given by:
$L = f_o + f_e = 105 \mathrm{~cm}$

Substituting $f_o$:
$20 f_e + f_e = 105 \mathrm{~cm}$
$21 f_e = 105 \mathrm{~cm} \Rightarrow f_e = 5 \mathrm{~cm} = 0.05 \mathrm{~m}$

Then, the focal length of the objective is:
$f_o = 20 \times 5 = 100 \mathrm{~cm} = 1 \mathrm{~m}$

The optical power of a lens is $P = \dfrac{1}{f(\text{in meters})}$.

Power of the objective:
$P_o = \dfrac{1}{1} = +1 \mathrm{~D}$

Power of the eyepiece:
$P_e = \dfrac{1}{0.05} = +20 \mathrm{~D}$

Therefore, the powers of the objective and eyepiece are $+1 \mathrm{~D}$ and $+20 \mathrm{~D}$ respectively.

Answer: $+1 \mathrm{~D}$ and $+20 \mathrm{~D}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object is placed at a distance of $20\text{ cm}$ in front of a combination of two thin lenses in contact. A real image is formed at a distance of $30\text{ cm}$ from the combination. The first lens is equiconvex with a refractive index of $1.5$ and a radius of curvature of $30\text{ cm}$ for both surfaces. If the second lens is plano-convex with a radius of curvature of $12\text{ cm}$ for its curved surface, what is the refractive index of the material of the second lens?
questions.solution:
Using the thin lens formula for the combination to find its equivalent focal length $F$:
$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{F}$
$\dfrac{1}{+30} - \dfrac{1}{-20} = \dfrac{1}{F}$
$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{30} + \dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{5}{60} = \dfrac{1}{12}\text{ cm}^{-1}$

Using the lens maker's formula to find the focal length of the first equiconvex lens $f_1$:
$\dfrac{1}{f_1} = (\mu_1 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{-R_1}\right)$
$\dfrac{1}{f_1} = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{2}{30}\right) = 0.5 \times \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{1}{30}\text{ cm}^{-1}$

The equivalent focal length of two thin lenses in contact is given by:
$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{f_1} + \dfrac{1}{f_2}$
$\dfrac{1}{12} = \dfrac{1}{30} + \dfrac{1}{f_2}$
$\dfrac{1}{f_2} = \dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{5 - 2}{60} = \dfrac{3}{60} = \dfrac{1}{20}\text{ cm}^{-1}$

Using the lens maker's formula for the second plano-convex lens to find its refractive index $\mu_2$:
$\dfrac{1}{f_2} = (\mu_2 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_2} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right)$
$\dfrac{1}{20} = (\mu_2 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{12}\right)$
$\mu_2 - 1 = \dfrac{12}{20} = 0.6$
$\mu_2 = 1.6$

Answer: $1.6$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two lenses, A and B, are made of the same transparent material. Lens A is an equiconvex lens with both surfaces having a radius of curvature $R$. Lens B is a biconvex lens with surfaces having radii of curvature $R$ and $2R$. The ratio of the power of lens A to the power of lens B ($P_A : P_B$) is:
questions.solution:
The power of a lens is given by the Lens Maker's formula:
$P = \dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$

For lens A (equiconvex), $R_1 = R$ and $R_2 = -R$:
$P_A = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \left(-\dfrac{1}{R}\right)\right) = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{2}{R}\right)$

For lens B (biconvex), $R_1 = R$ and $R_2 = -2R$:
$P_B = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \left(-\dfrac{1}{2R}\right)\right) = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} + \dfrac{1}{2R}\right) = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{3}{2R}\right)$

Taking the ratio of their powers:
$\dfrac{P_A}{P_B} = \dfrac{(\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{2}{R}\right)}{(\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{3}{2R}\right)} = \dfrac{2}{3/2} = \dfrac{4}{3}$

Thus, the ratio $P_A : P_B$ is $4:3$.

Answer: $4:3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Effective Power of two thin lenses in contact(I) $P_1 + P_2$
(B) Effective Focal Length of two thin lenses in contact(II) $\dfrac{f_1 f_2}{f_1 + f_2}$
(C) Effective Magnification of two thin lenses in contact(III) $m_1 \times m_2$
(D) Effective Power of a convex and a concave lens of equal focal lengths in contact(IV) Zero

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
When two thin lenses are placed in contact, their effective power is the algebraic sum of their individual powers: $P_{\text{net}} = P_1 + P_2$.

The effective focal length $f_{\text{net}}$ is given by $\dfrac{1}{f_{\text{net}}} = \dfrac{1}{f_1} + \dfrac{1}{f_2}$, which simplifies to $f_{\text{net}} = \dfrac{f_1 f_2}{f_1 + f_2}$.

The effective magnification of a combination of lenses is the product of their individual magnifications: $m_{\text{net}} = m_1 \times m_2$.

For a convex lens (positive focal length $f$) and a concave lens (negative focal length $-f$) of equal focal lengths in contact, the effective power is $P_{\text{net}} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \left(-\dfrac{1}{f}\right) = 0$.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A student plots a graph of the angle of deviation ($\delta$) versus the angle of incidence ($i$) for a monochromatic light ray passing through an equilateral prism. The lowest point on the plotted curve has coordinates $(x, y)$. If the refractive index of the prism material is $\sqrt{3}$, what are the values of $x$ and $y$ respectively?
questions.solution:
The graph of the angle of deviation ($\delta$) versus the angle of incidence ($i$) is a curve where the lowest point corresponds to the position of minimum deviation.

At this lowest point, the coordinates $(x, y)$ represent the angle of incidence at minimum deviation ($i_m$) and the minimum angle of deviation ($\delta_m$) respectively.

For an equilateral prism, the angle of the prism is $A = 60^\circ$. At minimum deviation, the angle of refraction is $r = \dfrac{A}{2} = 30^\circ$.

Using Snell's law to find the angle of incidence $x = i_m$:

$\sin i_m = \mu \sin r$

$\sin i_m = \sqrt{3} \sin 30^\circ = \sqrt{3} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

This gives $i_m = 60^\circ$. Thus, $x = 60^\circ$.

The minimum angle of deviation $y = \delta_m$ is given by the formula:

$\delta_m = 2i_m - A$

$\delta_m = 2(60^\circ) - 60^\circ = 120^\circ - 60^\circ = 60^\circ$

Thus, $y = 60^\circ$.

The coordinates $(x, y)$ are $(60^\circ, 60^\circ)$.

Answer: $(60^\circ, 60^\circ)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An extended object of height $2\text{ cm}$ is placed perpendicular to the principal axis at a distance of $60\text{ cm}$ from a convex lens of focal length $20\text{ cm}$. A plane mirror is placed perpendicular to the principal axis at a distance of $20\text{ cm}$ behind the lens. What are the height and the nature of the final image formed after the second refraction through the lens?
questions.solution:
For the first refraction through the convex lens:
$u = -60\text{ cm}$, $f = +20\text{ cm}$
$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_1} = \dfrac{1}{20} + \dfrac{1}{-60} = \dfrac{2}{60} \Rightarrow v_1 = +30\text{ cm}$
Magnification $m_1 = \dfrac{v_1}{u} = \dfrac{30}{-60} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$

This image $I_1$ is formed $30\text{ cm}$ to the right of the lens. Since the plane mirror is at $20\text{ cm}$, $I_1$ is $10\text{ cm}$ behind the mirror, acting as a virtual object for it.
The plane mirror forms a real image $I_2$ at $10\text{ cm}$ in front of it (i.e., $10\text{ cm}$ to the right of the lens).
Magnification of plane mirror $m_2 = +1$.

For the second refraction through the lens, light travels from right to left. The object $I_2$ is at $10\text{ cm}$ from the lens.
Applying sign convention for this reversed direction: $u_2 = -10\text{ cm}$, $f = +20\text{ cm}$
$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{f} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_2} = \dfrac{1}{20} + \dfrac{1}{-10} = -\dfrac{1}{20} \Rightarrow v_2 = -20\text{ cm}$
Since $v_2$ is negative, the final image is formed on the side of the incident light (to the right of the lens), making it a virtual image.
Magnification $m_3 = \dfrac{v_2}{u_2} = \dfrac{-20}{-10} = +2$

Total magnification $m = m_1 \times m_2 \times m_3 = \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \times (+1) \times (+2) = -1$
Final height $= |m| \times h_o = |-1| \times 2\text{ cm} = 2\text{ cm}$. The negative sign indicates the final image is inverted.

Answer: $2\text{ cm}$, virtual and inverted

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ray of monochromatic light passes through an equilateral prism such that the refracted ray inside the prism is parallel to its base. If the angle of deviation of the ray is $60^\circ$, what is the critical angle of the prism material with respect to air?
questions.solution:
For an equilateral prism, the angle of the prism is $A = 60^\circ$.

The refracted ray is parallel to the base, meaning the prism is in the position of minimum deviation. In this state, the angle of refraction is $r = \dfrac{A}{2} = 30^\circ$.

The angle of deviation is given as $\delta = 60^\circ$. Using the formula for minimum deviation:
$\delta = 2i - A$
$60^\circ = 2i - 60^\circ$
$2i = 120^\circ \Rightarrow i = 60^\circ$

The refractive index of the prism material is:
$\mu = \dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r} = \dfrac{\sin 60^\circ}{\sin 30^\circ} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{\dfrac{1}{2}} = \sqrt{3}$

The critical angle $\theta_c$ of the prism material with respect to air is given by:
$\sin \theta_c = \dfrac{1}{\mu}$
$\sin \theta_c = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$
$\theta_c = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$.

Answer: $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A light ray is incident on one face of a prism of refracting angle $60^{\circ}$. The refractive index of the material of the prism is $\sqrt{\dfrac{7}{3}}$. If the ray undergoes grazing emergence at the second face, the angle of incidence is:
questions.solution:
At the second face, for grazing emergence, the angle of refraction is $90^{\circ}$.

Thus, the angle of incidence at the second face is the critical angle $c$.
$\sin c = \dfrac{1}{\mu} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{7}}$
$\cos c = \sqrt{1 - \sin^2 c} = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{3}{7}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{7}}$

For a prism, $r_1 + r_2 = A$. Here $r_2 = c$ and $A = 60^{\circ}$.
$r_1 = 60^{\circ} - c$

Applying Snell's law at the first face:
$\sin i = \mu \sin r_1 = \mu \sin(60^{\circ} - c)$
$\sin i = \mu (\sin 60^{\circ} \cos c - \cos 60^{\circ} \sin c)$
$\sin i = \sqrt{\dfrac{7}{3}} \left( \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{7}} - \dfrac{1}{2} \times \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{7}} \right)$
$\sin i = \sqrt{\dfrac{7}{3}} \left( \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{7}} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{7}} \right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{7}{3}} \left( \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{7}} \right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Therefore, $i = 30^{\circ}$.

Answer: $30^{\circ}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A right-angled prism has acute angles of $30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$. A ray of monochromatic light is incident normally on the face adjacent to the $90^\circ$ and $30^\circ$ angles. The ray strikes the hypotenuse and emerges into the surrounding air. If the angle of emergence from the hypotenuse is $45^\circ$, what is the refractive index of the material of the prism?
questions.solution:
The ray is incident normally on the face adjacent to the $90^\circ$ and $30^\circ$ angles. Therefore, it enters the prism undeviated and travels parallel to the base (the face adjacent to the $90^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ angles).

When the ray strikes the hypotenuse, the angle between the hypotenuse and the base is $60^\circ$. Since the ray is parallel to the base, the angle between the incident ray and the hypotenuse is also $60^\circ$.

The angle of incidence $i$ is measured from the normal to the surface. Thus, $i = 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ$.

Applying Snell's law at the hypotenuse:
$\mu \sin(i) = 1 \times \sin(e)$
$\mu \sin(30^\circ) = \sin(45^\circ)$
$\mu \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
$\mu = \sqrt{2}$

Using $60^\circ$ as the angle of incidence is a common mistake that leads to $\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}$.

Answer: $\sqrt{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object is placed at a distance of $30$ cm in front of a convex lens of focal length $20$ cm. A concave lens of focal length $10$ cm is placed coaxially behind the convex lens at a distance $d$. If the final image formed by the combination is at infinity, the value of $d$ is :
questions.solution:
For the convex lens:
Object distance, $u_1 = -30$ cm
Focal length, $f_1 = +20$ cm
Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{f_1}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{-30} = \dfrac{1}{20}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_1} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{3 - 2}{60} = \dfrac{1}{60}$
$\Rightarrow v_1 = +60$ cm
The image formed by the convex lens acts as a virtual object for the concave lens.

For the concave lens:
The final image is at infinity, so $v_2 = \infty$.
Focal length, $f_2 = -10$ cm
Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{f_2}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{\infty} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{-10}$
$\Rightarrow 0 - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = -\dfrac{1}{10}$
$\Rightarrow u_2 = +10$ cm

The virtual object is $10$ cm to the right of the concave lens. Since it was formed $60$ cm to the right of the convex lens, the separation distance $d$ between the lenses is:
$d = v_1 - u_2 = 60 - 10 = 50$ cm.

Answer: $50$ cm

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A plano-convex lens made of a material with a refractive index of $1.5$ has a power of $+5\text{ D}$. The radius of curvature of its curved surface is:
questions.solution:
The power of the lens is $P = +5\text{ D}$.

The focal length $f$ in meters is given by $f = \dfrac{1}{P} = \dfrac{1}{5}\text{ m} = 20\text{ cm}$.

For a plano-convex lens, the radius of curvature of the plane surface is $R_2 = \infty$, and let the curved surface be $R_1 = R$.

Using the Lens Maker's formula:
$\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$

Substitute the values:
$\dfrac{1}{20} = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right)$

$\dfrac{1}{20} = 0.5 \times \dfrac{1}{R}$

$R = 20 \times 0.5 = 10\text{ cm}$.

Answer: $10\text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
An astronomical telescope in normal adjustment is constructed using two convex lenses of optical powers $+0.5 \mathrm{~D}$ and $+25 \mathrm{~D}$. Match the parameters of the telescope in List-I with their corresponding values in List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Tube length(I) $200 \mathrm{~cm}$
(B) Magnitude of magnifying power(II) $4 \mathrm{~cm}$
(C) Focal length of objective(III) $204 \mathrm{~cm}$
(D) Focal length of eyepiece(IV) $50$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
For an astronomical telescope, the objective lens must have a larger focal length and the eyepiece must have a smaller focal length.

Given powers:
$P_1 = +0.5 \mathrm{~D}$ and $P_2 = +25 \mathrm{~D}$

Focal lengths are:
$f_1 = \dfrac{1}{P_1} = \dfrac{1}{0.5} \mathrm{~m} = 2 \mathrm{~m} = 200 \mathrm{~cm}$
$f_2 = \dfrac{1}{P_2} = \dfrac{1}{25} \mathrm{~m} = 0.04 \mathrm{~m} = 4 \mathrm{~cm}$

Thus, focal length of objective, $f_o = 200 \mathrm{~cm}$ (C → I)
Focal length of eyepiece, $f_e = 4 \mathrm{~cm}$ (D → II)

In normal adjustment, the tube length is:
$L = f_o + f_e = 200 + 4 = 204 \mathrm{~cm}$ (A → III)

Magnitude of magnifying power is:
$|m| = \dfrac{f_o}{f_e} = \dfrac{200}{4} = 50$ (B → IV)

Correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ray of monochromatic light is incident on an equilateral prism made of a material of refractive index $\sqrt{2}$. The ray undergoes refraction such that the light ray inside the prism travels parallel to its base. The angle of deviation of the ray is :
questions.solution:
For an equilateral prism, the angle of the prism is $A = 60^\circ$.

The refracted ray inside the prism is parallel to its base, which indicates that the prism is in the position of minimum deviation.

In this position, the angle of refraction is $r = \dfrac{A}{2} = \dfrac{60^\circ}{2} = 30^\circ$.

Applying Snell's law at the first refracting surface:
$\mu = \dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r}$
$\sqrt{2} = \dfrac{\sin i}{\sin 30^\circ}$
$\sin i = \sqrt{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

This gives the angle of incidence $i = 45^\circ$.

The angle of deviation $\delta$ in the position of minimum deviation is given by:
$\delta = 2i - A$
$\delta = 2(45^\circ) - 60^\circ = 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ$.

Answer: $30^\circ$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object is placed at a distance of $30$ cm in front of a convex lens of focal length $20$ cm. A convex mirror is placed coaxially $20$ cm behind the lens. If the final image formed by the combination coincides with the object itself, the focal length of the convex mirror is :
questions.solution:
For the convex lens:
Object distance, $u = -30$ cm
Focal length, $f = +20$ cm
Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{-30} = \dfrac{1}{20}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{60}$
$\Rightarrow v = +60$ cm
The convex lens forms an image $60$ cm to its right.

The convex mirror is placed $20$ cm behind the lens. The image formed by the lens acts as a virtual object for the mirror, located at a distance of $60 - 20 = 40$ cm behind the mirror.

For the final image to coincide with the object, the rays refracted by the lens must strike the convex mirror normally. This means the rays must be directed towards the center of curvature of the mirror.
Therefore, the center of curvature is at the position of the virtual object, which is $40$ cm behind the mirror.
Radius of curvature, $R = 40$ cm.
The focal length of the convex mirror is $f_m = \dfrac{R}{2} = \dfrac{40}{2} = 20$ cm.

Answer: $20$ cm

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An astronomical telescope has an objective of focal length $150 \text{ cm}$ and an eyepiece of focal length $5 \text{ cm}$. It is initially focused on a distant star in normal adjustment. The observer then adjusts the eyepiece to refocus the telescope so that the final image forms at the least distance of distinct vision ($25 \text{ cm}$). What is the magnitude and direction of the displacement of the eyepiece?
questions.solution:
In normal adjustment, the final image is formed at infinity. The object for the eyepiece (the intermediate image formed by the objective) lies exactly at its principal focus.
$u_{e1} = f_e = 5 \text{ cm}$
The initial tube length is $L_1 = f_o + f_e = 150 + 5 = 155 \text{ cm}$.

When the telescope is adjusted so the final image is at the least distance of distinct vision ($v_e = -25 \text{ cm}$), we use the lens formula for the eyepiece to find the new object distance $u_{e2}$:
$\dfrac{1}{v_e} - \dfrac{1}{u_{e2}} = \dfrac{1}{f_e}$
$\dfrac{1}{-25} - \dfrac{1}{u_{e2}} = \dfrac{1}{5}$
$\dfrac{1}{u_{e2}} = -\dfrac{1}{25} - \dfrac{1}{5} = -\dfrac{6}{25}$
$u_{e2} = -\dfrac{25}{6} \text{ cm} \approx -4.17 \text{ cm}$

The new tube length is $L_2 = f_o + |u_{e2}| = 150 + \dfrac{25}{6} = 154.17 \text{ cm}$.

The displacement of the eyepiece is the difference in tube lengths:
$\Delta L = L_1 - L_2 = 5 - \dfrac{25}{6} = \dfrac{5}{6} \text{ cm}$.

Since the required tube length has decreased ($L_2 \lt L_1$), the eyepiece must be moved closer to the intermediate image, which means it is moved towards the objective.

Answer: $\dfrac{5}{6} \text{ cm}$ towards the objective

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ray of light is incident at an angle of $2^{\circ}$ on one face of a thin prism of prism angle $5^{\circ}$. If the refractive index of the material of the prism is $1.6$, then the angle of emergence of the ray is
questions.solution:
For a thin prism, the angle of deviation $\delta$ is given by:
$\delta = (\mu - 1)A$
$\delta = (1.6 - 1) \times 5^{\circ} = 0.6 \times 5^{\circ} = 3^{\circ}$

The general relation between the angle of incidence $i$, angle of emergence $e$, prism angle $A$, and deviation $\delta$ is:
$i + e = A + \delta$

Substituting the given values:
$2^{\circ} + e = 5^{\circ} + 3^{\circ}$
$2^{\circ} + e = 8^{\circ}$
$e = 6^{\circ}$

Alternatively, using the small angle approximation directly:
$i + e = \mu A$
$2^{\circ} + e = 1.6 \times 5^{\circ}$
$2^{\circ} + e = 8^{\circ}$
$e = 6^{\circ}$

Answer: $6^{\circ}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A right-angled prism (refracting angle $A = 90^{\circ}$) is completely immersed in a transparent liquid of refractive index $\sqrt{2}$. A light ray hits one face of the prism at an angle of incidence of $45^{\circ}$ and emerges grazing the second face. The refractive index of the prism glass is:
questions.solution:
Let the refractive index of the prism be $\mu_g$ and that of the liquid be $\mu_L = \sqrt{2}$.

At the first face, applying Snell's law:
$\mu_L \sin i = \mu_g \sin r_1$

At the second face, the ray grazes the surface, so the angle of refraction is $90^{\circ}$ and the angle of incidence is the critical angle $c$ for the glass-liquid interface:
$\mu_g \sin c = \mu_L \sin 90^{\circ} \Rightarrow \sin c = \dfrac{\mu_L}{\mu_g}$

For a prism, $r_1 + c = A$. Given $A = 90^{\circ}$, we have $r_1 = 90^{\circ} - c$.
Therefore, $\sin r_1 = \sin(90^{\circ} - c) = \cos c = \sqrt{1 - \sin^2 c} = \sqrt{1 - \left(\dfrac{\mu_L}{\mu_g}\right)^2}$.

Substituting this into the first Snell's law equation:
$\mu_L \sin i = \mu_g \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{\mu_L^2}{\mu_g^2}} = \sqrt{\mu_g^2 - \mu_L^2}$

Squaring both sides:
$\mu_L^2 \sin^2 i = \mu_g^2 - \mu_L^2$
$\mu_g^2 = \mu_L^2 (1 + \sin^2 i)$

Given $\mu_L = \sqrt{2}$ and $i = 45^{\circ}$:
$\mu_g^2 = (\sqrt{2})^2 \left(1 + \sin^2 45^{\circ}\right) = 2 \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 2 \times \dfrac{3}{2} = 3$

Thus, $\mu_g = \sqrt{3}$.

Answer: $\sqrt{3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A thin equiconvex glass lens of refractive index $1.5$ and radius of curvature $20\text{ cm}$ for both surfaces is placed horizontally on a plane glass slab. A few drops of an unknown liquid are squeezed between the lens and the slab, forming a plano-concave liquid lens. If the equivalent focal length of this combination is $30\text{ cm}$, what is the refractive index of the liquid?
questions.solution:
The focal length $f_g$ of the equiconvex glass lens is calculated using the lens maker's formula:
$\dfrac{1}{f_g} = (\mu_g - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$
$\dfrac{1}{f_g} = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{-20}\right) = 0.5 \times \dfrac{2}{20} = \dfrac{1}{20}\text{ cm}^{-1}$

The liquid forms a plano-concave lens. For light travelling downwards, its upper surface matches the lower surface of the glass lens ($R_1 = -20\text{ cm}$) and its lower surface is plane ($R_2 = \infty$).
The focal length $f_l$ of the liquid lens is:
$\dfrac{1}{f_l} = (\mu_l - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{-20} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right) = -\dfrac{\mu_l - 1}{20}$

The equivalent focal length of the combination is $F = 30\text{ cm}$.
$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{f_g} + \dfrac{1}{f_l}$
$\dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{\mu_l - 1}{20}$
$\dfrac{\mu_l - 1}{20} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{60}$
$\mu_l - 1 = \dfrac{20}{60} = \dfrac{1}{3}$
$\mu_l = 1 + \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}$

Answer: $4/3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A light ray is incident at an angle $i$ on one face of a prism of refracting angle $A$. The ray emerges grazing the second face. Which of the following is the correct algebraic expression for the refractive index $\mu$ of the prism material?
questions.solution:
Let $r_1$ be the angle of refraction at the first face and $c$ be the angle of incidence at the second face.
For grazing emergence, the angle of incidence at the second face is the critical angle $c$, so $\sin c = \dfrac{1}{\mu}$ and $\cos c = \dfrac{\sqrt{\mu^2 - 1}}{\mu}$.

For a prism, $r_1 + c = A \Rightarrow r_1 = A - c$.

Applying Snell's law at the first face:
$\sin i = \mu \sin r_1$
$\sin i = \mu \sin(A - c)$
$\sin i = \mu (\sin A \cos c - \cos A \sin c)$

Substituting the expressions for $\sin c$ and $\cos c$:
$\sin i = \mu \left( \sin A \dfrac{\sqrt{\mu^2 - 1}}{\mu} - \cos A \dfrac{1}{\mu} \right)$
$\sin i = \sin A \sqrt{\mu^2 - 1} - \cos A$

Rearranging to solve for $\mu$:
$\sin i + \cos A = \sin A \sqrt{\mu^2 - 1}$
$\sqrt{\mu^2 - 1} = \dfrac{\sin i + \cos A}{\sin A}$

Squaring both sides:
$\mu^2 - 1 = \left( \dfrac{\sin i + \cos A}{\sin A} \right)^2$
$\mu = \sqrt{1 + \left( \dfrac{\sin i + \cos A}{\sin A} \right)^2}$

Answer: $\sqrt{1 + \left( \dfrac{\sin i + \cos A}{\sin A} \right)^2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When a convex lens is cut into two identical halves along its principal axis, the focal length of each half becomes half of the original value, and the intensity of the image remains unchanged.

Reason (R): When cut along the principal axis, the radii of curvature of the lens remain unchanged, while the aperture area is halved.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
The focal length of a lens is given by the Lens Maker's formula: $\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$.

When a lens is cut along its principal axis, the radii of curvature ($R_1$ and $R_2$) of the two halves remain the same as that of the original lens. Therefore, the focal length of each half remains unchanged. The Assertion states that the focal length becomes half, which is incorrect.

Furthermore, the intensity of the image formed by a lens is directly proportional to its aperture area. Since cutting the lens along the principal axis halves its aperture area, the amount of light passing through is halved, reducing the intensity of the image. The Assertion states that intensity remains unchanged, which is also incorrect.

The Reason correctly states that the radii of curvature remain unchanged and the aperture area is halved. Thus, the Assertion is false, but the Reason is true.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A fish in a pond looks at a bird flying vertically above in the air. To the fish, the bird appears to be at a greater height from the water surface than its actual height.
Reason (R): The apparent height $h'$ of an object at actual height $h$ in a rarer medium of refractive index $n_1$, when viewed from a denser medium of refractive index $n_2$, is given by $h' = h \left(\dfrac{n_1}{n_2}\right)$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Evaluate the Assertion (A):
When an object in a rarer medium (air) is viewed from a denser medium (water), the apparent height is given by $h' = h \times \dfrac{n_{\text{observer}}}{n_{\text{object}}}$.
Here, $n_{\text{observer}} = n_{\text{water}}$ and $n_{\text{object}} = n_{\text{air}}$. Since $n_{\text{water}} \gt n_{\text{air}}$, the apparent height $h'$ is greater than the actual height $h$. Thus, the bird appears to be at a greater height. The Assertion (A) is true.

Evaluate the Reason (R):
The general formula for apparent height/depth is $h' = h \left(\dfrac{n_{\text{observer}}}{n_{\text{object}}}\right)$.
In the given scenario, the observer is in the denser medium ($n_2$) and the object is in the rarer medium ($n_1$).
Therefore, the correct formula should be $h' = h \left(\dfrac{n_2}{n_1}\right)$.
The Reason states $h' = h \left(\dfrac{n_1}{n_2}\right)$, which is incorrect. The Reason (R) is false.

Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
An object is placed at $x = -30$ cm on the principal axis of a coordinate system. A convex lens $L_1$ of focal length $20$ cm is fixed at the origin ($x = 0$). A second lens $L_2$ is placed at $x = +30$ cm. Match the specifications of lens $L_2$ in List-I with the x-coordinate of the final image in List-II.

List-I (Lens $L_2$)List-II (Final image position)
(A) Convex, $f = +15$ cm(I) $x = 0$ cm
(B) Concave, $f = -15$ cm(II) $x = +40$ cm
(C) Concave, $f = -30$ cm(III) $x = +45$ cm
(D) Convex, $f = +30$ cm(IV) $x = \infty$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
For the first lens $L_1$ (convex lens at $x = 0$):
Object distance, $u_1 = -30$ cm
Focal length, $f_1 = +20$ cm
Using the lens formula: $\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{-30} = \dfrac{1}{20}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_1} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{3 - 2}{60} = \dfrac{1}{60}$
$\Rightarrow v_1 = +60$ cm
The image from $L_1$ is formed at $x = +60$ cm.

For the second lens $L_2$ (placed at $x = +30$ cm):
The image formed by $L_1$ acts as a virtual object for $L_2$.
Object distance for $L_2$, $u_2 = +60 - 30 = +30$ cm.

Evaluating each case in List-I:
(A) Convex, $f = +15$ cm:
$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{15} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_2} = \dfrac{1}{15} + \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{3}{30} = \dfrac{1}{10} \Rightarrow v_2 = +10$ cm.
Final coordinate $x = 30 + 10 = +40$ cm. (Matches II)

(B) Concave, $f = -15$ cm:
$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{-15} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_2} = -\dfrac{1}{15} + \dfrac{1}{30} = -\dfrac{1}{30} \Rightarrow v_2 = -30$ cm.
Final coordinate $x = 30 - 30 = 0$ cm. (Matches I)

(C) Concave, $f = -30$ cm:
$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{-30} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_2} = -\dfrac{1}{30} + \dfrac{1}{30} = 0 \Rightarrow v_2 = \infty$.
Final coordinate $x = \infty$. (Matches IV)

(D) Convex, $f = +30$ cm:
$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{30} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_2} = \dfrac{1}{30} + \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{2}{30} = \dfrac{1}{15} \Rightarrow v_2 = +15$ cm.
Final coordinate $x = 30 + 15 = +45$ cm. (Matches III)

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I describes different optical configurations involving glass lenses ($\mu = 1.5$) with a radius of curvature of $20\text{ cm}$ for their curved surfaces. List-II gives the equivalent focal length of the system.

List-IList-II
(A) An equiconvex lens in air(I) $+10\text{ cm}$
(B) Two such equiconvex lenses placed in contact in air(II) $-100\text{ cm}$
(C) Two plano-convex lenses placed with their curved surfaces facing each other, and the gap filled with a liquid of $\mu = 1.6$(III) Infinity
(D) The equiconvex lens completely immersed in a liquid of $\mu = 1.5$(IV) $+20\text{ cm}$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) For the equiconvex lens in air:
$\dfrac{1}{f_A} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{-R}\right) = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{2}{20}\right) = \dfrac{1}{20}\text{ cm}^{-1} \Rightarrow f_A = +20\text{ cm}$.

(B) For two such lenses in contact:
$\dfrac{1}{f_B} = \dfrac{1}{f_A} + \dfrac{1}{f_A} = \dfrac{1}{20} + \dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{2}{20} = \dfrac{1}{10}\text{ cm}^{-1} \Rightarrow f_B = +10\text{ cm}$.

(C) The combination consists of two plano-convex lenses and a biconcave liquid lens in the middle.
Focal length of each plano-convex lens: $\dfrac{1}{f_p} = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{20}\right) = \dfrac{1}{40}\text{ cm}^{-1}$.
Focal length of the liquid lens: $\dfrac{1}{f_L} = (1.6 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{-20} - \dfrac{1}{20}\right) = 0.6 \times \left(-\dfrac{2}{20}\right) = -\dfrac{6}{100}\text{ cm}^{-1}$.
Equivalent focal length: $\dfrac{1}{f_C} = \dfrac{1}{f_p} + \dfrac{1}{f_L} + \dfrac{1}{f_p} = \dfrac{1}{40} - \dfrac{6}{100} + \dfrac{1}{40} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{6}{100} = \dfrac{5 - 6}{100} = -\dfrac{1}{100}\text{ cm}^{-1} \Rightarrow f_C = -100\text{ cm}$.

(D) When immersed in a liquid of the same refractive index ($\mu = 1.5$):
$\dfrac{1}{f_D} = \left(\dfrac{1.5}{1.5} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{2}{20}\right) = 0 \Rightarrow f_D = \infty$.

Hence, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A converging beam of light is directed towards a point P. A concave lens of focal length $15$ cm is placed in the path of the beam such that point P is $10$ cm behind the concave lens. A convex lens of focal length $20$ cm is placed $10$ cm behind the concave lens. The final image formed by the combination is located at:
options: $80$ cm in front of the convex lens
questions.solution:
For the first lens (concave lens):
The converging beam is directed towards point P, which acts as a virtual object.
Object distance, $u_1 = +10$ cm
Focal length, $f_1 = -15$ cm
Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{f_1}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{1}{-15}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_1} = \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{3 - 2}{30} = \dfrac{1}{30}$
$\Rightarrow v_1 = +30$ cm
The intermediate image is formed $30$ cm behind the concave lens. This acts as a virtual object for the second lens.

For the second lens (convex lens):
Distance between the lenses, $d = 10$ cm
Object distance for the convex lens, $u_2 = v_1 - d = 30 - 10 = +20$ cm (virtual object)
Focal length, $f_2 = +20$ cm
Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{f_2}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{1}{20}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_2} = \dfrac{1}{20} + \dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{2}{20} = \dfrac{1}{10}$
$\Rightarrow v_2 = +10$ cm

The positive sign indicates that the final image is formed $10$ cm behind (to the right of) the convex lens.

Answer: $10$ cm behind the convex lens

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Light enters the flat circular end of an optical fiber at an angle of incidence of $60^{\circ}$. The ray then hits the curved side wall exactly at the critical angle, resulting in grazing emergence into the surrounding air cladding. The refractive index of the fiber core is:
questions.solution:
Let the refractive index of the fiber core be $\mu$ and the angle of refraction at the flat end be $r$.

Applying Snell's law at the flat entry surface:
$1 \times \sin 60^{\circ} = \mu \sin r$
$\sin r = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2\mu}$

Inside the fiber, the ray strikes the curved side wall. From the geometry of the cylinder, the normal to the side wall is perpendicular to the normal at the flat end. Thus, the angle of incidence at the side wall is $90^{\circ} - r$.

For grazing emergence into the air cladding, this angle must equal the critical angle $c$.
$\sin(90^{\circ} - r) = \sin c = \dfrac{1}{\mu}$
$\cos r = \dfrac{1}{\mu}$

Using the trigonometric identity $\sin^2 r + \cos^2 r = 1$:
$\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2\mu}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{1}{\mu}\right)^2 = 1$
$\dfrac{3}{4\mu^2} + \dfrac{1}{\mu^2} = 1$
$\dfrac{7}{4\mu^2} = 1 \Rightarrow \mu^2 = \dfrac{7}{4}$

$\mu = \dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A plano-convex lens is made of a material with a refractive index of $1.5$. If the radius of curvature of its curved surface is $25\text{ cm}$, what is the power of the lens?
questions.solution:
According to the Lens Maker's formula, the focal length $f$ is given by:

$\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$

For a plano-convex lens, the radius of curvature of the curved surface is $R_1 = +25\text{ cm} = +0.25\text{ m}$, and the plane surface has an infinite radius of curvature, so $R_2 = \infty$.

Substituting the given values:

$\dfrac{1}{f} = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{0.25} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right)$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = 0.5 \times 4 = 2\text{ m}^{-1}$

The power of the lens is $P = \dfrac{1}{f}$ (with $f$ in meters).

Therefore, $P = +2\text{ D}$.

Answer: $+2\text{ D}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An equiconcave lens is made of glass with a refractive index of $1.5$. If the radius of curvature of each of its surfaces is $20\text{ cm}$, what is the power of the lens?
questions.solution:
For an equiconcave lens, the radii of curvature are $R_1 = -20\text{ cm}$ and $R_2 = +20\text{ cm}$.

Using the Lens Maker's formula:
$\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$

Substitute the given values:
$\dfrac{1}{f} = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{-20} - \dfrac{1}{20}\right)$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = 0.5 \times \left(-\dfrac{2}{20}\right) = -\dfrac{1}{20}\text{ cm}^{-1}$

The focal length is $f = -20\text{ cm} = -0.2\text{ m}$.

The power of the lens is given by $P = \dfrac{1}{f(\text{in m})}$.

$P = \dfrac{1}{-0.2} = -5\text{ D}$.

Answer: $-5\text{ D}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A combination of a thin convex lens of power $+5\text{ D}$ and a thin concave lens of power $-5\text{ D}$ placed in contact produces a linear magnification of $+1$ for any object distance.
Reason (R): The effective power of this combination is zero, making it behave like a plane glass plate.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is not correct
Assertion (A) is not correct but Reason (R) is correct
questions.solution:
The effective power of the lens combination is the algebraic sum of their individual powers:
$P_{\text{net}} = P_1 + P_2 = +5\text{ D} + (-5\text{ D}) = 0\text{ D}$.

Since $P_{\text{net}} = 0$, the effective focal length $F = \dfrac{1}{P_{\text{net}}} = \infty$.
A lens system with infinite focal length behaves like a plane glass plate. Reason (R) is correct.

Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{F} = 0 \implies v = u$.
The linear magnification is $m = \dfrac{v}{u} = \dfrac{u}{u} = +1$.
Thus, the combination produces a magnification of $+1$ for any object distance. Assertion (A) is correct.

Reason (R) provides the exact physical basis (zero power and infinite focal length) for why the magnification is $+1$. Therefore, both statements are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

When an object is placed in front of such a lens,the rays first of all refracted from the convex surface, then refract from the polished plane surface and again refracts from convex surface. If $f_l$ and $f_m$ be the focal lengths of lens (convex surface) and mirror (plane polished surface) respectively, then effective focal length $F$ is given by
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{F}=\frac{1}{f_l}+\frac{1}{f_m}+\frac{1}{f_l}=\frac{2}{f_l}+\frac{1}{f_m}=\frac{2}{f_l} \quad\left(\because f_m=\frac{R}{2}=\infty\right) \\ & \frac{1}{f_l}=(\mu-1)\left(\frac{1}{R}\right) \\ & \therefore \frac{1}{F}=\frac{2(\mu-1)}{R} \text { or } F=\frac{R}{2(\mu-1)} \text { or } R=2 F=\frac{R}{(\mu-1)}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An isotropic point source of light is suspended $h$ metre vertically above the centre of circular table of radius $r$ metre. Then, the ratio of illumenances at the centre to that at the edge of the table is
questions.solution: According to question, the situation is shown in the figure below $E_1=\frac{I}{(L O)^2}=\frac{I}{h^2}...(i)$ The illumination at the edge $A$ is given by $E_2=\frac{I \cos \theta}{(L A)^2}=\frac{I \cos \theta}{\left(h^2+r^2\right)}...(ii)$ From figure, $\cos \theta=\frac{h}{\sqrt{\left(h^2+r^2\right)}}\therefore E_2=\frac{I h}{\left(h^2+r^2\right)^{3 / 2}}$ Dividing Eq. (i) by Eq. (ii), we get $\begin{aligned}\frac{E_1}{E_2} & =\frac{I / h^2}{I h /\left(h^2+r^2\right)^{3 / 2}}=\frac{\left(h^2+r^2\right)^{3 / 2}}{h^3} \\ & =\left(\frac{h^2+r^2}{h^2}\right)^{3 / 2}=\left(1+\frac{r^2}{h^2}\right)^{3 / 2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A fish rising vertically to the surface of water in a lake uniformly at the rate of $2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ observes a kingfisher diving vertically towards the water at a rate of $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. If refractive index of water $n=\frac{4}{3}$, what will be the actual velocity of the kingfisher
questions.solution: $\because$ Velocity of bird w.r.t. fish, $v_{B \rightarrow F}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ and velocity of fish w.r.t. ground $V_{F \rightarrow G}=2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\therefore$ Distance between bird and fish, as seen by fish $S=x+n y$ on differentiating w.r.t. time, we get $\begin{aligned} & \frac{d S}{d t}=\frac{d x}{d t}+n \frac{d y}{d t} \\ & v_{B \rightarrow F}=v_{F \rightarrow G}+n \cdot v_{B \rightarrow G} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 10=2+\frac{4}{3} v_{B \rightarrow G} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad v_{B \rightarrow G}=\frac{8}{4 / 3}=6 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\ & \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A square wire of side 2.0 cm is placed 20 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm with its centre on the axis of the mirror and its plane normal to the axis. The area enclosed by the image of wire is
questions.solution:
Given, square wire of side $=2 \mathrm{~cm}$, $u=-20 \mathrm{~cm}, f=-10 \mathrm{~cm}$,
Area of second wire $=$ ?
$\begin{aligned} & \therefore & \frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{u} & =\frac{1}{f} \\ & \Rightarrow & \frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{(-20)} & =\frac{1}{-10} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{v}=-\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{20} \\ & \Rightarrow & v & =-20 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$
We know that, $m=-\frac{v}{u}=\frac{-(-20)}{-20}=-1\because \quad \frac{\text { Area of image }}{\text { Area of object }}=m^2 \Rightarrow \frac{A_i}{A_0}=(-1)^2\frac{A_i}{2 \times 2}=1\Rightarrow \quad A_i=4 \mathrm{~cm}^2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A quarter cylinder of radius $R$ and refractive index 1.5 is placed on a table. A point object $P$ is kept at a distance of $m R$ from it as shown in figure. For what value of $m$ for which a ray from $P$ will emerge parallel to the table?
questions.solution: Refraction at plane surface (1), $n_1=1, n_2=1.5=\frac{3}{2}, u=-m R, v=?$ Using formula, $\frac{n_2}{v}-\frac{n_1}{u}=\frac{n_2-n_1}{R}\begin{aligned} & \because \quad R=\infty \text { for plane surface. } \\ & \because \frac{3 / 2}{v}-\frac{1}{(-m R)}=0 \\ & \therefore \quad v=-\frac{3}{2} m R\end{aligned}$ Refraction at spherical surface (2) $\begin{aligned} & u=-\left(\frac{3}{2} m R+R\right) \text { and } R=-R, v=\infty, \\ & n_1=\frac{3}{2}, n_2=1\end{aligned}\frac{1}{\infty}-\frac{3 / 2}{\left[-\left(\frac{3}{2} m R+R\right)\right]}=\frac{1-3 / 2}{-R}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{3 / 2}{\frac{R(3 m+2)}{2}}=\frac{1 / 2}{R} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{6}{3 m+2}=1 \Rightarrow 3 m+2=6 \\ & m=\frac{4}{3} \\ & \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnification produced by a astronomical telescope for normal adjustment is 10 and the length of the telescope is 1.1 m . The magnification, when the image is formed atleast distance of distinct vision is
questions.solution:
Given, $m=10$, length of telescope $=1.1 \mathrm{~m}$
We know that,
Magnification, $m=\frac{t_0}{t_e}\begin{aligned} & 10=\frac{t_0}{t_e} \\ & f_0=10 f_e \\ & \because \quad f_e+f_0=1.1 \mathrm{~m} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad t_e+10 t_e=1.1 \mathrm{~m} \\ & {\left[\because f_0=10 f_e\right]} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad f_e(1+10)=1.1 \mathrm{~m} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad f_e=0.1 \mathrm{~m} \text { or } 10 \mathrm{~cm} \\ & \end{aligned}$
Magnification least distance of distinct vision,
$\begin{aligned} M_b & =\frac{f_o}{f_e}\left(1+\frac{f_e}{D}\right) \\ & =10\left(1+\frac{10}{25}\right) \quad[\because D=25 \mathrm{~cm}] \\ & =10 \times \frac{35}{25} \\ & =14\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A prism of a certain angle deviates the red and blue rays by 8 and 12 , respectively. Another prism of the same angle deviates the red and blue rays by 10 and 14 , respectively. The prisms are small angled and made of different materials. The dispersive power of the materials of the prisms are in the ratio
questions.solution:
For prism 1,
$\begin{aligned} & \delta=\frac{\delta_B+\delta_R}{2}=\frac{12+8}{2}=10 \\ & \text { [given, } \delta_R=8, \delta_B=12 \text { ] } \\ & \therefore \quad \omega_1=\frac{\delta_B-\delta_R}{\delta}=\frac{12-8}{10}=\frac{4}{10}=\frac{2}{5} \\ & \end{aligned}$
For prism 2,
$\begin{aligned} & \delta=\frac{\delta_B+\delta_R}{2}=\frac{14+10}{2}=12 \\ \therefore \quad & \omega_2=\frac{\delta_B-\delta_R}{\delta}=\frac{14-10}{12}=\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}$
So, $\quad \frac{\omega_1}{\omega_2}=\frac{2 / 5}{1 / 3}=\frac{6}{5}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A vessel of depth $t$ is half filled with a liquid having refractive index $n_1$ and the other half is filled with water of having refractive index $n_2$. The apparent depth of the vessel as viewed from top is
